about: How each of Orsino's trap mechanisms (orsino-world.json) is understood and dealt with in a generated work: what is noticed of it in passing (sign), what looking closely at it shows (seen), and the ways of making it safe, each with what it needs. Written by hand: Orsino gives a trap's mechanism and what it does, not how it is found out or got past. Each calling has an answer to some of them and none to all: a thief's trapwork and a pole for what is set by hand, a scholar's lore and a priest's rites for what is written, a warrior's strength for what can be lifted, a ranger's eye for a snare, a monk's stride (the play-structure audit's PT-20: every trap had the same two answers, and a lone mage with neither walked into it).

pressure plate.sign: One flag of the floor across the way is not quite level with the others, and there is no dust in the crack round it.
pressure plate.seen: One flag of the floor sits a finger's breadth proud of the rest, with no dust in the crack round it. A foot's weight on it would set off whatever it is joined to; so would any weight.

ways.label: Lean on the plate with the pole, standing well back
Wedge the plate so it cannot sink
Heave the flag up out of its bed and lay it aside
Cross the plate in one long stride from the flag before it

tripwire.sign: Something catches the light low across the way: a wire, at the height of an ankle.
tripwire.seen: The wire runs from a peg at one side to a hole in the stone at the other. Whatever it works is behind the hole. Pull it, or catch a foot in it, and it goes.

ways.label: Hook the wire with the pole and pull, from well back
Pin the wire slack against the floor and step over it
Step the wire as you would a snare-line, high and slow

hidden switch.sign: The wall here is carved all over, and the carving is thickest where the way is narrowest.
hidden switch.seen: Among the carvings is one that is not carved but set in, a boss that would go in under a hand. It sits where a hand leaning on the wall would find it, at the narrowest place.

ways.label: Push the switch in with the pole's end, standing clear
Wedge the switch so it cannot go in
Read which of the carvings is set in, and keep your hands from it
Find where the carving is worn by hands that knew to miss the switch, and miss it too

arcane glyph.sign: A glyph is cut in the wall beside the way, and it shimmers faintly, as if it had only just been written.
arcane glyph.seen: The glyph is a word, written to be read by whoever passes it; reading it is what sets it off. Someone who knew the letters could unsay it.

ways.label: Unsay the glyph, letter by letter
Hold the pole's end across the glyph, looking away
Speak the rite that ends what was begun, and cover the glyph

magical rune.sign: A rune is laid in the floor across the way, its lines lit with a dull glow that comes and goes, slow as breathing.
magical rune.seen: The rune is laid in the floor where a foot must cross it. It is waiting for weight, or warmth; it cannot tell the one from the other.

ways.label: Break the rune's lines with the right words
Lay the pole's end on the rune from as far off as it allows
Speak over the rune the rite that lays such things to rest

enchanted object.sign: Something stands in the way that has no business there: an ordinary-looking thing that hums when you come near it.
enchanted object.seen: The thing is set exactly where anyone going through must knock against it. Whatever is in it is waiting to be knocked over; a pole would do it as well as a passing hip.

ways.label: Knock it over with the pole, from well back
Say over it what quiets such things
Bless it, and carry it aside while the blessing holds
Lift it whole, slowly, and set it down out of the way
